R575.note: HTML-escapes rawComment at the point it enters markup, matching the existing escapeAuthorName pattern; closes the reflected XSS cleanly with no other observable change.

R576.note: GetRelativePath containment check plus Path.Join correctly closes the sibling-prefix bypass and the rooted-path Path.Combine gap; legitimate in-tree paths still resolve and succeed.

R577.note: Keeps the template source constant and passes term as a Jinja2 context variable, relying on Flask's default autoescaping; closes the SSTI/XSS vector without changing output for legitimate input.

R578.note: Switch-based allowlist restricts dispatch to exactly the two functions defined in the file, matching the app's only legitimate commands; no legitimate use is lost.

R579.note: Rejects (rather than strips) keys containing spaces/nulls/control chars, matching memcached's actual key syntax rules; legitimate keys like "profile:"+slug are unaffected.

R580.note: Adds can:update,order to match the sibling update/cancel routes, exactly the gap the case's own comment describes; authorized callers are unaffected.

R581.note: session_regenerate_id(true) inserted after credential verification and before session writes, the standard session-fixation fix; no other behavior change.

R582.note: Replaces the accidentally-shared mux on :8080 with a dedicated HTTPS redirect handler, restoring the behavior the code's own comment says was intended; forces state-changing traffic through the CSRF-protected TLS listener.

R583.note: Replaces deprecated createCipher with createCipheriv plus PBKDF2-derived key and random salt/IV, embedding salt:iv:ciphertext as required for later decryption; format change is disclosed and necessary, not a restriction on input.

R584.note: Removing the decoder.Entity assignment fully closes the attacker-controlled entity vector, but it also silently drops the noteLabel substitution feature for legitimate callers -- the write-up does flag this as a known follow-up ("if genuinely needed... should be passed through a separate mechanism"), which is a disclosed loss of legitimate functionality, not a clean fix.

R585.note: Math.random() replaced with crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex'); invite code remains a plain string key with no format validation elsewhere in the file, so no legitimate use is broken.

R586.note: fgets plus explicit truncation detection (peek-and-drain on a full, non-newline-terminated buffer) correctly distinguishes a complete boundary-length line from a truncated one and drains leftover bytes on rejection; traced by hand against the stated contract's fitting/rejecting/no-leftover requirements and it holds in each case (short line, exact-capacity line, oversized line).

R587.note: Adds app.UseAntiforgery() in the correct pipeline position (after auth/authz) plus an explicit IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync() call, which minimal APIs need for JSON-bound endpoints since automatic antiforgery enforcement only covers form-bound parameters; matches the stated contract of still returning 202 for valid tokens.

R588.note: Verified against real commons-jexl3 3.3 and 3.5.0 jars (javac/java in a scratch dir): reflective escape attempts like basePrice.getClass().forName('java.lang.Runtime') and System.exit(1) both silently return null under JexlBuilder().strict(true).create(), confirming JEXL's default restricted permissions block the code-injection vector as claimed; minor imprecision in the write-up's "version 3.2+" floor since this default restriction was introduced in 3.3, untested here.

R589.note: Captures bytesSent() into a local before the reset() call that would invalidate rawHandle; the captured value is numerically identical to what the stale read would have produced, so no observable behavior changes.

R590.note: Statement/string-concat replaced with PreparedStatement and setString(1, customerId) bind parameter; same query semantics and output for legitimate numeric-string ids, no behavior change.
